name: fransushi
description: FranSushi: free MIT plugins for orchestrated multi-worker coding with Claude Code. Developed and shipped inside template_harness (claude/).

plugins.name: sushibuild
plugins.description: Hand a build to a Haiku triage subagent. It runs your build command, routes each small local error to a Sonnet fixer that may edit exactly one file (enforced by a hook), logs every fixup, and escalates anything big back to you with the build log.

plugins.name: sushicomms
plugins.description: Typed handoff and question tickets between workers: a role registry the coordinator edits, validated ticket files, a monitor that prints one line when every handoff of a batch is in, and reminders when a command breaks a role rule.

plugins.name: sushidelivery
plugins.description: Urgency-tagged, phone-readable decision reports for Claude Code, plus an optional, off-by-default relay of permission prompts and multiple-choice questions to your own Telegram bot or ntfy topic. Prefer Remote Control and the official channel plugins first.

plugins.name: sushirice
plugins.description: Build slots and machine protection: builds wait for a free slot and live headroom (load, memory pressure, compiler count); an opt-in guard pauses your own newest compiler processes under pressure; reuse analysis flags needless rebuilds.

plugins.name: sushistyle
plugins.description: House coding rules as tested clang AST matchers. Light inline reminders after each C/C++ edit; a hard gate for CI. The clang tier runs on a build host you name, never on the machine hosting Claude.

plugins.name: sushiwrap
plugins.description: Worker records (seats) that keep a worker's role, track, branch, worktree and resume note in files; host-reset deadlines with shutdown checklists 30, 15 and 5 minutes before the reset; a shutdown lint; and host survey/provision manifests.

plugins.name: wasabi
plugins.description: Guard hooks for Bash: protect shared working trees from stash/switch/clean/commit -a, stop mass CRLF staging, ask before dependency downloads, and warn about commands that will hang on stdin.
